BERT4Rec’s random masked-item objective and terminal next-item inference expose different contexts; terminal coverage alone cannot establish historical training allocation or optimization influence. The [original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) establishes Cloze training, while [2024 encoder-only recommendation research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.11150) explores Sequential Masked Modeling. These motivate checking supervision provenance, but do not recover missing sampler logs or demonstrate gradient conflict in this model.

Practical instrumentation proposal: persist category, step, sampled user/prefix endpoint, truncation, selected target positions, terminal/interior membership, corruption type, branch coefficients, and exact loss numerators/denominators. Distinguish pooled target means from separately normalized branch means: their optimization weights differ even with identical target counts. For class-index cross-entropy, ignored targets are excluded from the mean denominator; class weighting changes it to the sum of applicable target weights. Record actual implemented reduction, not an inferred denominator ([PyTorch CrossEntropyLoss](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss.html)).

At sparse diagnostic steps, partition the existing loss into terminal/interior contributions using its original denominator and coefficients. Obtain gradients from the same forward graph with `torch.autograd.grad(..., retain_graph=True)`, which returns gradients without accumulating parameter `.grad`; then run the unchanged training backward/optimizer step. Log weighted gradient norms and pairwise cosine separately for shared item embeddings and encoder parameters, marking zero-norm cosines undefined. Negative cosine indicates local first-order conflict, not proven validation harm ([gradient-conflict research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.06782)). Preserve dropout realization, RNG, sampling and context; detach logged values. These are proposed measurements, not recovered evidence, and add compute while retaining one jointly trained BERT4Rec per category ([autograd documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.autograd.grad)).
